---
title: "Case study: South America"
subtitle: "Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Colombia – where German demand is linked to the loss of natural ecosystems, and why it changes"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/setup.R")

focus <- c(BRA = "Brazil", ARG = "Argentina", PRY = "Paraguay", COL = "Colombia")
p0 <- periods[2]             # 2000–2005, reference period of the case study
p1 <- latest_period          # latest period
p_first <- periods[1]        # 1995–2000, larger uncertainties

sa <- ct %>% filter(subregion == "South America")

# region totals and share of the global footprint
sa_period <- sa %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  summarise(bfnee_km2 = sum(bfnee_km2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(global_period %>% select(period, global_km2 = bfnee_km2), by = "period") %>%
  mutate(share = bfnee_km2 / global_km2)
sa_at <- function(p) sa_period %>% filter(period == p)

# focus countries: drivers per period
drv <- sa %>%
  filter(iso3 %in% names(focus)) %>%
  transmute(iso3, country = unname(focus[iso3]), period,
            bfnee_km2, loss_constrained_km2,
            gain_crop = agri_gain_cropland_km2, gain_past = agri_gain_pasture_km2,
            weight = ifelse(loss_constrained_km2 > 0, bfnee_km2 / loss_constrained_km2, NA_real_)) %>%
  mutate(country = factor(country, levels = unname(focus)))
dv <- function(iso, p, var) drv %>% filter(iso3 == iso, period == p) %>% pull({{ var }})
chg <- function(iso, var) dv(iso, p1, {{ var }}) / dv(iso, p0, {{ var }}) - 1

# focus countries: ecosystem groups
eco <- ce %>%
  filter(iso3 %in% names(focus)) %>%
  group_by(iso3, period, eco_group) %>%
  summarise(bfnee_km2 = sum(bfnee_km2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(iso3, period) %>%
  mutate(share = bfnee_km2 / sum(bfnee_km2)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(country = factor(unname(focus[iso3]), levels = unname(focus)))
es <- function(iso, p, g) {
  v <- eco %>% filter(iso3 == iso, period == p, eco_group == g) %>% pull(share)
  if (length(v) == 0) 0 else v
}

# focus countries: commodities
com <- cc %>%
  filter(iso3 %in% names(focus)) %>%
  group_by(iso3, period, commodity_label) %>%
  summarise(bfnee_km2 = sum(bfnee_km2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(iso3, period) %>%
  mutate(share = bfnee_km2 / sum(bfnee_km2)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(country = factor(unname(focus[iso3]), levels = unname(focus)))
cs <- function(iso, p, lab) {
  v <- com %>% filter(iso3 == iso, period == p, commodity_label == lab) %>% pull(share)
  if (length(v) == 0) 0 else v
}
oil <- label_commodity("Oil bearing crops")

pct <- function(x) fmt_pct(abs(x))
```

{{< include _approx-note.qmd >}}

South America was the main hotspot of the footprint during the soy and cattle boom
of the early 2000s. This page compares four producing countries in which German
demand is linked to the loss of natural ecosystems in very different ways. It is
the online version of the case study in the public monitoring report; all numbers
are calculated from the tables of this website.

## South America in the global footprint

```{r}
#| label: fig-sa-region
#| fig-cap: !expr 'cap("BF-NEE in South America per five-year period, in km², by producing country. The four case-study countries are shown individually, the other six South American countries are combined. The label above each bar is the region’s share of the global BF-NEE.")'
#| fig-height: 4.4
reg <- sa %>%
  mutate(country = ifelse(iso3 %in% names(focus), unname(focus[iso3]), "Other South America"),
         country = factor(country, levels = rev(c(unname(focus), "Other South America")))) %>%
  group_by(period, country) %>%
  summarise(bfnee_km2 = sum(bfnee_km2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

country_cols <- c(Brazil = "#1c5cab", Argentina = "#3987e5", Paraguay = "#86b6ef",
                  Colombia = "#eda100", `Other South America` = bf_ink$other)

p <- ggplot(reg, aes(period, bfnee_km2, fill = country,
                     text = paste0(country, "<br>", period, ": ", fmt_km2(bfnee_km2)))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(data = sa_period, aes(period, bfnee_km2, label = fmt_pct(share)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.5, size = 3.4, colour = bf_ink$secondary) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = country_cols, name = NULL, breaks = names(country_cols)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fmt_area, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "BF-NEE in South America",
       subtitle = "By producing country; label = share of the global footprint",
       x = NULL, y = "BF-NEE (km²)")

bf_interactive(p)
```

In `r p0` the region accounted for `r fmt_km2(sa_at(p0)$bfnee_km2)`, or
`r fmt_pct(sa_at(p0)$share)` of the footprint of German final demand; by `r p1`
this had fallen to `r fmt_km2(sa_at(p1)$bfnee_km2)` (`r fmt_pct(sa_at(p1)$share)`).
Values for `r p_first` are shown for completeness but are subject to larger
uncertainties in the input data, so trends are described from `r p0` onwards.

## Which ecosystems are lost?

```{r}
#| label: fig-sa-eco
#| fig-cap: !expr 'cap("BF-NEE of German final demand in Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Colombia by ecosystem group and five-year period, in km². Each panel has its own y-axis scale.")'
#| fig-height: 5.4
p <- ggplot(eco %>% filter(bfnee_km2 > 0),
            aes(period, bfnee_km2, fill = eco_group,
                text = paste0(country, " · ", eco_group, "<br>", period, ": ",
                              fmt_km2(bfnee_km2), " (", fmt_pct(share), ")"))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ country, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = eco_group_colors, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = fmt_area, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(title = "BF-NEE by ecosystem group",
       subtitle = "Each panel has its own scale",
       x = NULL, y = "BF-NEE (km²)") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8))

bf_interactive(p, height = 600) |>
  plotly::layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2, yanchor = "top"))
```

## Less conversion or less trade?

BF-NEE changes for two reasons: how much natural land is converted for agriculture
in the producing country (agriculture-constrained loss), and how much of that
country's production is linked to German final demand (the attribution weight,
BF-NEE ÷ constrained loss). The figure separates the two.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sa-drivers
#| fig-cap: !expr 'cap("Change between ", p0, " and ", p1, " in the agriculture-constrained natural ecosystem loss (conversion on the ground), in the attribution weight (share of the loss linked to German final demand, BF-NEE ÷ constrained loss) and in BF-NEE, per country, in percent. Colombia’s increase in constrained loss is cut off at +200 % for readability; the exact values are given in the labels and the table below.")'
#| fig-height: 4.2
dchg <- drv %>%
  filter(period %in% c(p0, p1)) %>%
  select(country, period, `Constrained loss` = loss_constrained_km2,
         `Attribution weight` = weight, `BF-NEE` = bfnee_km2) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(country, period), names_to = "measure") %>%
  group_by(country, measure) %>%
  summarise(change = value[period == p1] / value[period == p0] - 1, .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = c("Constrained loss", "Attribution weight", "BF-NEE")),
         shown = pmin(change, 2))

ggplot(dchg, aes(shown, country, fill = change > 0)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = bf_ink$axis) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%+.0f %%", 100 * change),
                hjust = ifelse(change > 0, -0.15, 1.15)),
            size = 3.2, colour = bf_ink$secondary) +
  facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#d03b3b", `FALSE` = "#1c5cab"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = c("−100", "0", "+100", "+200"),
                     limits = c(-1.7, 3.1), breaks = c(-1, 0, 1, 2)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(title = paste("What changed between", p0, "and", p1, "?"),
       subtitle = "Red = increase, blue = decrease",
       x = "Change (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bfnee(grid = "x")
```

## Four countries, four stories

**Brazil – rising again after 2010, and moving into savannas.** After a low in
`r periods[3]` (`r fmt_km2(dv("BRA", periods[3], bfnee_km2))`), the footprint rose to
`r fmt_km2(dv("BRA", p1, bfnee_km2))` in `r p1`, because cropland expansion more
than tripled and a larger share of production was linked to German demand.
Savannas (`r fmt_pct(es("BRA", p1, "Savanna"))`) and shrublands
(`r fmt_pct(es("BRA", p1, "Shrubland"))`) now dominate; forests account for
`r fmt_pct(es("BRA", p1, "Forest"))`. `r oil` carry
`r fmt_pct(cs("BRA", p1, oil))` of the footprint.

**Argentina – strongest decline.** The footprint fell by
`r pct(chg("ARG", bfnee_km2))` compared with `r p0`, as both conversion
(−`r pct(chg("ARG", loss_constrained_km2))`, mainly less pasture expansion) and the
share of production linked to Germany (−`r pct(chg("ARG", weight))`) decreased.

**Paraguay – less conversion, but from forests to shrublands.** The footprint fell
by `r pct(chg("PRY", bfnee_km2))` because less land was converted, while the trade
link to Germany remained stable. The forest share dropped from
`r fmt_pct(es("PRY", p0, "Forest"))` to `r fmt_pct(es("PRY", p1, "Forest"))`,
shrublands rose to `r fmt_pct(es("PRY", p1, "Shrubland"))`; `r tolower(oil)` carry
`r fmt_pct(cs("PRY", p1, oil))` of the footprint.

**Colombia – the only rising footprint.** It more than doubled
(+`r pct(chg("COL", bfnee_km2))`) because conversion grew almost fivefold,
driven by the expansion of intensive pasture (from
`r fmt_km2(dv("COL", p0, gain_past))` to `r fmt_km2(dv("COL", p1, gain_past))`),
mostly at the expense of forests (`r fmt_pct(es("COL", p1, "Forest"))`).

## Which products?

```{r}
#| label: fig-sa-commodities
#| fig-cap: !expr 'cap("Share of BF-NEE by commodity in each case-study country in ", p1, ". Commodity groups follow LandSHIFT; soy is part of oil-bearing crops and maize part of cereals. Loss linked to the expansion of intensive pasture is attributed to grazing livestock.")'
#| fig-height: 3.8
d <- com %>% filter(period == p1, bfnee_km2 > 0)

p <- ggplot(d, aes(share, country, fill = commodity_label,
                   text = paste0(country, " · ", commodity_label, "<br>",
                                 fmt_km2(bfnee_km2), " (", fmt_pct(share), ")"))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = commodity_colors_lab, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(title = paste("BF-NEE by commodity,", p1),
       subtitle = "Share of each country's footprint",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_bfnee(grid = "x")

bf_interactive(p) |>
  plotly::layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.15, yanchor = "top"))
```

## Why this matters for policy

Progress towards target 21.1 of the German National Biodiversity Strategy 2030 –
reducing the negative impacts of global supply chains on biodiversity – is currently
considered not measurable. BF-NEE can close this gap: it shows where, in which
ecosystems and through which products German consumption is linked to the loss of
natural ecosystems, and whether changes result from less conversion on the ground
or from shifts in trade. The South American cases show that both drivers matter and
can point in opposite directions. Because savannas, shrublands and grasslands
account for a large part of the footprint in Brazil and Paraguay, a forest-only view –
as in the EU Deforestation Regulation – misses much of it.

## Data

```{r}
drv %>%
  transmute(Country = country, Period = period,
            `Constrained loss (km²)` = round(loss_constrained_km2),
            `Cropland expansion (km²)` = round(gain_crop),
            `Intensive pasture expansion (km²)` = round(gain_past),
            `Attribution weight` = signif(weight, 3),
            `BF-NEE (km²)` = round(bfnee_km2, 1)) %>%
  arrange(Country, Period) %>%
  bf_table(page_length = 16) %>%
  DT::formatRound(c("Constrained loss (km²)", "Cropland expansion (km²)",
                    "Intensive pasture expansion (km²)"), digits = 0) %>%
  DT::formatRound("BF-NEE (km²)", digits = 1)
```

Constrained loss = natural ecosystem loss that coincides with agricultural expansion
in the same grid cell and period. Attribution weight = BF-NEE ÷ constrained loss,
i.e. the share of the loss linked to German final demand through the commodities
grown on the new land.
